name: Claude Code sandbox (default-deny egress + persistent auth)
description: Installs Claude Code, a default-deny egress firewall, and a persistent state volume, so that running the agent with --dangerously-skip-permissions has a bounded blast radius.

firewall.description: Lock egress down to the allowlist at container start. Turning this off leaves the container with open networking: the filesystem is still contained, but anything readable is exfiltratable.

allowedDomains.description: Extra domains to allow, space- or comma-separated. These are your toolchain's hosts: package registries, mirrors, internal services. Anthropic's own hosts are always allowed.

githubRanges.description: Allow GitHub's published IP ranges, fetched from api.github.com/meta. More durable than resolving the hostnames, because git operations land on addresses a single A record never sees.

installClaudeCode.description: Install Claude Code with the native installer. Turn off if the base image already carries it.

version.description: Which Claude Code build to install: 'stable', 'latest', or an exact x.y.z version.

installUtilities.description: Install the tools Claude Code reaches for rather than shelling out: ripgrep, git, jq, less, procps, unzip.

seedOnboarding.description: Pre-answer the first-run wizard and trust the workspace folder, so a --rm run goes straight to the prompt instead of a login screen.

permissionMode.description: Default permission mode seeded into settings.json. acceptEdits auto-approves file edits but still asks before running commands; bypassPermissions asks nothing (pair it with acceptBypassPermissions).

acceptBypassPermissions.description: Pre-accept the --dangerously-skip-permissions warning, for sessions launched in bypass mode. Off by default: the seeded default is acceptEdits, which never shows that warning.

restrictSudo.description: Remove blanket NOPASSWD sudo grants the base image gave the remote user (devcontainers/base images grant NOPASSWD:ALL), leaving only the firewall entry. Without this, the agent can sudo iptables -F and the egress rules are decorative.
